record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Given a pattern p, what is the complexity of deciding whether p is avoidable?

evidence.quote: Given a pattern p, what is the complexity of deciding whether p is avoidable? With regard to k-avoidability itself, three open problems were stated:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet of letters and let E be a disjoint countably infinite alphabet of variables. A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ E*. An occurrence of p in a word w ∈ A* is the image h(p) of p under a non-erasing morphism h : E* → A* such that h(p) is a factor of w. An infinite word w over A is said to avoid p if no factor of w is an occurrence of p. The pattern p is called avoidable if there exists some finite alphabet A and some infinite word over A that avoids p; otherwise p is called unavoidable.

It is known (Bean–Ehrenfeucht–McNulty, Zimin) that avoidability of patterns is decidable. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem:

  Input: a pattern p ∈ E*.
  Question: is p avoidable?

That is, determine the precise complexity class (e.g., in P, NP-complete, coNP-complete, PSPACE-complete, etc.) of deciding pattern avoidability.
artifact.status_search_result: Deciding whether a pattern is unavoidable is known to be coNP-complete (equivalently, deciding avoidability is NP-complete), as established for the unavoidability problem and reported in recent work on "The Complexity of Unavoidable Word Patterns" (Theory of Computing Systems, 2022). However, fine-grained questions about the complexity of avoidability for restricted classes of patterns and related variants remain active. The general decidability question has long been answered, while the precise complexity classification matching upper and lower bounds appears settled at NP-completeness for the basic version.

status_evidence.title: The Complexity of Unavoidable Word Patterns
status_evidence.snippet: The computational complexity of determining whether a word pattern is unavoidable has been investigated, with a proof that this problem is NP-complete (equivalently coNP-complete for unavoidability depending on formulation).
status_evidence.claim: The complexity of deciding (un)avoidability of word patterns has been determined to be NP-complete.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorics on Words – A Tutorial (Berstel, Karhumäki)
status_evidence.snippet: An algorithm to decide whether a pattern is avoidable was given independently by Bean, Ehrenfeucht, and McNulty (1979) and Zimin (1982).
status_evidence.claim: Avoidability of patterns is decidable, but the problem's exact complexity class was an open question.
